rows.title: loom.repository-read-in-invariant — a repo read in an invariant emits an undefined identifier wrapped around a TAUTOLOGY on 4 backends and is dropped entirely on elixir
Repo.run(<Retrieval>) in a paged queryHandler crashes the emitter after 0 error(s) — promote the internal throw to a validator refusal
loom.containment-cycle — a self-recursive entity part validates clean then RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded on node/dotnet/python/elixir
Reserved-name gate so an emitter-owned name (dotnet nested `State`) is refused at the model, not at dotnet build
typescript/emit/aggregate.ts:487 emits `private <fn>` while when-guards, can_<op> routes and workflow bodies call it — TS2341
nestedContainLoads recursion bound (belt-and-braces alongside the P1 gate)
emit/entity.ts:702 emits a nested `public sealed class State` on every aggregate; a field named `state` collides — CS0102 + CS0542. docs/language.md prints this exact model as a legal example.
emit/entity.ts:426 emits `private` for an aggregate function called from CloseHandler/CanCloseHandler — CS0122
An entity named `...Exception` fails CA1711 under the -warnaserror gate the generated .csproj configures; suppress alongside CA1707/CA1848/CA1873 which it already suppresses
`mask unless` emits Objects.equals(...) into <Agg>Response.java without `import java.util.Objects` — BUILD FAILED. The recommended remedy for PII exposure breaks the Java build.
emit/entity.ts:586 emits `private` for an aggregate function called from DocService/workflow service
emit/aggregate.ts defines `_has_skill` while workflows_routes.py calls `has_skill` — AttributeError at request time, NOT a convention issue
`"on " + self._start_at` is a TypeError on every read; the SAME generated file already writes self._start_at.isoformat() for inspect. Fix regardless of the RC-4 fork.
The datetime-coercion helper binds __dt/__s/__d/__other then uses them — 5 warnings, fails `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, a gate the README lists

All 5 backends pass ICU formats through (`i18nFormat: (inner) => inner`): {at,date} == {at,time}, ::currency drops, and a plural's arms VANISH (emits "3", not "3 items"). FORK: implement per backend, or add loom.interp-format-backend-only. docs/new-plan/T1 says the pass-through is deliberate; docs/language.md does not.

form-fields.ts initFor returns "null" for a collection -> FormControl<null> -> TS2345 under ng build. React degrades HONESTLY on the same model (disabled, translated '(arrays not yet supported in forms)'). The same function's comment already records this fix for the X id case.

A declared `retrieval` emits NO route while the deprecated `find` does. loom.repository-find-deprecated points authors at a construct that cannot reach the wire; the working replacement costs 4 declarations + an api{} block.
string -> enum emits NO migration and NO constraint (TEXT->TEXT). An out-of-enum row is then served against the API's own OpenAPI enum, which the same generation's zod client rejects.

ddd i18n init/sync produce locales/<locale>.json that `generate system` never reads; only en.json is emitted. The generated i18n.ts tells the user to hand-edit it — which F-012 then deletes. The three-way merge itself is good and should not be touched.

The OIDC audience check is emitted only when the model declares `audience:` — a clause present in ddd.langium:182 and ABSENT from docs/auth.md. All five backends default it off (python alone is env-enablable). The emitted comment asserts the check is on regardless. Executed: a same-issuer token for another client returns 200.
The generated keycloak realm ships no protocol mappers for the declared user{} claims, so the batteries-included IdP cannot exercise the tenancy the model declares
403 bodies echo the authorization predicate source verbatim; no flag suppresses it
README's Live site / playground / hosted docs are 404 after the org move; 5 lemmit.github.io + 6 github.com/lemmit/Loc URLs are dead
CLI --help points patch/trace/breakpoints at docs/old/proposals/**, which the README calls archived and un-deployed
`create { }` documented as valid ('omitting the parens keeps it quiet') and is a parse error; `destroy { }` works
A typo'd primitive type gives 'Could not resolve reference to NamedDecl named strng' — compiler-internal jargon, no did-you-mean, though the facility exists for field names
A soft keyword in expression position gives a raw Chevrotain dump: Unexpected 'from'. Expected one of: ... (+111 more)
docs/language.md presents ICU suffixes as general expression syntax WITH a backend TypeScript example; T1 says the backend drops them
Document the oidc `audience:` clause — it is in the grammar and nowhere in docs/auth.md

State the ownership model. 'The keys to the codebase' / 'All the source you'd write by hand' vs: a hand-edit is silently deleted on regenerate, and .loomignore freezes the file until the next model change breaks the build.

decisions.title: ICU on the backends: implement, or refuse with loom.interp-format-backend-only
decisions.note: docs/new-plan/T1 records the pass-through as deliberate. The python TypeError is a bug either way.

decisions.title: Source-ownership model: (1) own the compiler framing + emit a .gitignore, (2) hash-and-warn on clobber, (3) protected regions / three-way merge
decisions.note: Not an agent-sized fix. Option 1 is free; option 2 is the best value-per-unit-of-work and removes the SILENT half; option 3 is expensive and in tension with derive-don't-stamp.
